items.text: Temp service installed to Article 230 rules, with grounding and a working disconnect for every temporary circuit.
Removal date on the temp paperwork; temp comes out when the work it serves is done (holiday and decorative work: 90 days maximum).
GFCI protection on all 125V and 125/250V, 15A, 20A, and 30A receptacles used for the work, including permanent building receptacles being used temporarily; devices tested and logged.
Receptacles outside the direct GFCI list are GFCI protected or covered by a written assured grounding program with test records on site.
No receptacles on temporary lighting branch circuits; temp lighting on its own circuits.
All temp splices in boxes or enclosures with covers on; all temp lamps guarded.
Feeder and branch circuit cables supported off the ground and floor, protected at doorways and pinch points; wet-location receptacles weatherproof with a plug inserted.
Temp panel breakers inspected, listed for that panel, and not damaged or unknown-history takeouts.
Sharma temp panels use Siemens breakers listed for the panel; no mixed-brand swaps in temp gear.
Classification written on the takeoff for each space: major or minor repair, floor or pit or ceiling, ventilation provided or not.
Classified pockets wired to Article 501 methods; ordinary shop materials stop at the boundary.
Above the classified band, only the fixed methods listed in 511.7(A); luminaires over bays checked against the 12-foot conditions.
Under-slab runs detailed as 514-style underground work and settled before the pour.
GFCI protection per 210.8(B) on garage receptacles, tested at trim.
Vehicle charging scope, if any, identified separately with nameplate and ventilation information requested.
Commercial branch circuits 20A minimum on 12 AWG copper.
Datum plane established and marked on site before rough-in; nothing the article restricts set below it.
Service equipment for floating buildings located on adjacent land, not on the floating structure (Article 555, Part III — Article 553 was deleted in 2020).
All water-contact and energizable metal bonded with solid copper, 8 AWG minimum, back to the panelboard grounding bus; continuity tested.
Each shore power receptacle has an identified disconnect within 30 inches, readily accessible, ahead of the receptacle.
Receptacles at least 12 inches above finished deck and not below the datum plane; shore power only in listed marine power outlets.
GFPE layers set and recorded: shore power 30 mA maximum, dock feeder 100 mA maximum; other small receptacles Class A GFCI.
Tripping pedestal is investigated as a fault, never defeated or swapped to an ordinary breaker to keep a boat powered.
